description: Reviewable user decisions and proposed information requirements. Roles describe interests, not permissions or separate databases. Required tables/fields identify draft capabilities, not evidence of populated BOS source fields. Detailed means worked through for contract review, not implemented or source-validated. Candidate workflows expose missing capabilities and have no promised output projection. Steps are explanatory pseudo-code, not a query language.

workflows.title: Roof quantities by assembly
workflows.question: How much roof membrane and insulation does this building need, by assembly, and which roofs remain unmeasured?
workflows.decision: Prepare a measured bid scope and identify unresolved quantities before applying waste or pricing.

parameters.description: Explicit snapshot(s) and project/building scope; do not combine overlapping revisions as additional objects.
Named/versioned surface-area and deduction rules.
Requested layers or assembly definitions; never infer layer thickness from area.

steps.pseudocode: Select distinct whole-object, material-part or surface measurement subjects appropriate to the decision. Do not add overlapping whole-object and part quantities.
Select roof occurrences in the requested snapshot and building scope; retain unresolved location as an explicit scope exception.
Use the accepted net surface-area observation under the requested rule; do not substitute plan-projected area or sum competing observations.
Group compatible measured contributions by assembly; return measured subtotal, unmeasured roof count and exclusions. Report insulation volume only if its required thickness evidence is supplied.

workflows.missingDataBehavior: Unknown assembly or net surface area remains unresolved. Report supported partial quantities; do not treat unknown area as zero or diagnose exporter fault without evidence.
workflows.countingBasis: One selected measurement per roof occurrence and requested quantity basis; assembly totals and layer contributions are separate alternatives.
acceptanceExamples: Synthetic: a sloped roof with net surface area 120 m2 and projected area 100 m2 contributes 120 m2 to membrane area, not 220 m2.
Synthetic: a second roof with unknown area increases unmeasured count and leaves the measured subtotal unchanged.
openQuestions: Which opening-deduction and layer measurement standards should be supported first?
Roof edges, penetrations, drains and layer thickness are not yet dedicated contract projections.

workflows.title: Room-facing finish schedule
workflows.question: What finishes and net areas belong to each room-facing surface, including opposite sides of shared walls?
workflows.decision: Specify and measure finishes without assigning one room's finish to the other side of a shared component.

parameters.description: Explicit snapshot(s) and project/building scope; do not combine overlapping revisions as additional objects.
Requested spaces and surface/layer scope.
Named/versioned net-area deduction rule.

steps.pseudocode: Select distinct whole-object, material-part or surface measurement subjects appropriate to the decision. Do not add overlapping whole-object and part quantities.
Select room-facing surface contributions; preserve distinct sides of the same object.
Select supported finish observations using the named policy; keep conflicting observations discoverable and unresolved when no policy settles them.
Group compatible accepted net areas by space and finish; return unassigned surfaces and unmeasured contributions alongside totals.

workflows.missingDataBehavior: Unknown side, room association, finish or area is a separate unresolved contribution. Do not copy the sole known finish to another side.
workflows.countingBasis: One identified finish surface/side contribution; a wall may validly contribute to two spaces, but a repeated source representation is not an additional surface.
acceptanceExamples: Synthetic: one wall has north-room paint A at 12 m2 and south-room tile B at 10 m2; report two contributions, not two whole-wall totals.
Synthetic: conflicting finish observations return an unresolved finish until a selection rule is provided.
openQuestions: Does the first release require multiple finish layers, coat count and substrate preparation as explicit typed fields?
A stable surface identity and layer accounting rule still require source mapping validation.

workflows.title: Scenario-based package estimate
workflows.question: What does this trade package cost under the selected rates and waste assumptions, and what remains unpriced or uncertain?
workflows.decision: Compare bid scenarios while separating measured scope, omissions and unpriced quantities.

parameters.description: Explicit snapshot(s) and project/building scope; do not combine overlapping revisions as additional objects.
Selected package and explicitly included/excluded scope.
Versioned rate set, currency, date and region.
Explicit waste, contingency and rounding assumptions.

steps.pseudocode: Select distinct whole-object, material-part or surface measurement subjects appropriate to the decision. Do not add overlapping whole-object and part quantities.
Select package object scope and resolve overlaps under the counting policy.
Select compatible accepted quantities; match exactly one applicable rate from the requested reference version. Require dimensional and currency compatibility.
Apply declared scenario adjustments once; return priced subtotal, unpriced quantities and unresolved scope separately. Do not label a partial subtotal as a complete bid.

workflows.missingDataBehavior: No matching rate means unpriced, not free. Unknown quantities remain unknown; missing scope information prevents a completeness claim.
workflows.countingBasis: One priced scope contribution per scenario/rate basis; do not combine assembly price and constituent prices for the same scope.
acceptanceExamples: Synthetic: 10 m2 at 20 currency-units/m2 gives 200 before explicitly declared adjustments.
Synthetic: 5 m2 without a rate remains an unpriced line and does not become a zero-cost accepted line.
openQuestions: Where should scenario and currency metadata live as dedicated contract records?
How are alternates, provisional sums, allowances and partial package allocations represented?

workflows.title: Door delivery completeness audit
workflows.question: Which delivered doors lack the required fire-rating or usable clear-width evidence?
workflows.decision: Request corrections and identify unassessed requirements before accepting a delivery.

parameters.description: Explicit snapshot(s) and project/building scope; do not combine overlapping revisions as additional objects.
Versioned project requirements and applicability criteria; not inferred jurisdiction rules.

steps.pseudocode: Select identified door occurrences and applicable delivery scope; keep scope uncertainty visible.
For each supplied applicable requirement, distinguish usable values, conflicts, invalid observations, missing observations and supported evidence of non-applicability.
Emit pass/fail only with sufficient evidence and rule inputs; otherwise emit incomplete/unknown with reason. Exporter family alone cannot explain a missing field.

workflows.missingDataBehavior: Missing or invalid clear width is unassessed rather than compliant. Proven non-applicability is distinct from absent evidence; exporter omission requires documented support.
workflows.countingBasis: One assessment per door, requirement and selected delivery context; count assessed subjects separately from observation count.
acceptanceExamples: Synthetic: missing clear width under an applicable minimum-width requirement produces an incomplete/unknown outcome, never pass.
Synthetic: a documented non-applicable rating requirement is not a failing missing-property finding.
openQuestions: Requirement definitions and applicability predicates need an external/versioned contract.
Which distinctions between leaf size, nominal opening and usable clear width must be mandatory?

workflows.title: Supported service and connectivity trace
workflows.question: Which equipment and spaces are demonstrably connected to or served by this equipment, and where does the evidence stop?
workflows.decision: Understand supported service dependencies and plan an investigation of unresolved links.

parameters.description: Explicit snapshot(s) and project/building scope; do not combine overlapping revisions as additional objects.
Identified starting equipment or system.
Allowed relationship kinds, direction and evidence statuses.
Bounded traversal depth or explicit stop criteria.

steps.pseudocode: Select supported edges of explicitly requested kinds and direction; do not replace missing connectivity with geometric proximity.
Traverse with a visited-object set and stop criteria; retain each path's edge evidence and distinguish connected-to from serves.
Return supported reachable objects plus unresolved links and coverage limits. No observed path does not prove physical disconnection or safe isolation.

workflows.missingDataBehavior: An empty edge set yields no supported trace and unknown topology coverage. Inferred or uncertain edges are labeled and excluded from verified-only results.
workflows.countingBasis: Unique reachable objects within the selected snapshot; preserve multiple meaningful paths without counting the same asset repeatedly.
acceptanceExamples: Synthetic: A connects to B and B serves room C; a permitted mixed-kind trace returns B and C with their distinct relation meanings.
Synthetic: nearby object D with no supported edge is not connected by the trace.
openQuestions: Port-level topology, flow direction and operational isolation state require further explicit modeling.
The traversal result shape is illustrative; a dedicated path projection is not yet defined.

workflows.title: Material impact under a declared scenario
workflows.question: What embodied impact is attributable to these material quantities under the same factor version and lifecycle modules, and how much scope is unresolved?
workflows.decision: Compare material or procurement scenarios on a stated, comparable basis.

parameters.description: Explicit snapshot(s) and project/building scope; do not combine overlapping revisions as additional objects.
Versioned applicable environmental factors with units, geography and declared modules.
Explicit boundary, selected modules, substitutions and lifecycle assumptions.

steps.pseudocode: Select distinct whole-object, material-part or surface measurement subjects appropriate to the decision. Do not add overlapping whole-object and part quantities.
Select non-overlapping material contributions and accepted quantities for the selected objects and scenario.
Require an evidenced material/product-to-factor match and compatible declared quantity basis; an unsupported density conversion or name similarity is insufficient.
Compute compatible impacts for the selected modules and factor version; show unmatched quantities and coverage denominator. Do not sum aggregate-module factors with their constituent modules.

workflows.missingDataBehavior: Unmatched materials or incompatible quantity units yield unresolved impact. Unknown quantity or lifecycle coverage cannot be silently represented as zero.
workflows.countingBasis: One material contribution, factor selection and non-overlapping lifecycle module per scenario; deduplicate confirmed repeated source representations.
acceptanceExamples: Synthetic: 100 kg matched to 2 kgCO2e/kg yields 200 kgCO2e for the declared module.
Synthetic: a duplicate representation of that same confirmed contribution does not increase impact; an unmatched material stays unresolved.
openQuestions: Reference factor payloads, impact indicators and scenario boundaries need explicit contracts before execution.
How should biogenic carbon, reuse allocation and uncertainty intervals be represented?

workflows.title: Evidence coverage for a route-to-exit assessment
workflows.question: Can these spaces be assessed for a route to a designated exit, and which missing route, width or rule inputs block a conclusion?
workflows.decision: Prepare an explainable assessment and request missing inputs; avoid unsupported safety assurance.

parameters.description: Explicit snapshot(s) and project/building scope; do not combine overlapping revisions as additional objects.
Selected spaces, designated exits, occupancy and route assumptions.
Explicit versioned jurisdiction/project rules and applicability criteria.

steps.pseudocode: Require supported navigable space/portal topology, usable widths and supplied scenario/rule inputs; distinguish this graph from general physical adjacency.
If inputs support it, pass the explicitly scoped route graph and compatible spatial measurements to an identified assessment method. Candidate geometry alone cannot establish a usable path.
Report supported method results only for assessed scope; missing topology, obstacles or rule inputs keep the assessment incomplete. Do not claim whole-building safety from a partial graph.

workflows.missingDataBehavior: Missing paths are unresolved until topology coverage is established. Missing designated exits, occupancy, usable widths or applicable rules blocks a definitive outcome.
workflows.countingBasis: One assessment per subject and requirement in the scenario; multiple representations or candidate paths do not multiply occupants or assessed spaces.
acceptanceExamples: Synthetic: missing portal topology returns incomplete rather than 'no exit' or pass.
Synthetic: bounds touching two spaces does not establish a traversable portal.
openQuestions: Portals, navigable route geometry, travel-distance methods and scenarios are required future contracts.
Which narrowly scoped assessment should be validated first?

workflows.title: Maintainable asset and handover register
workflows.question: Where are our maintainable assets, which manuals are linked, and which handover requirements remain unresolved?
workflows.decision: Prioritize delivery corrections and locate assets without loading the whole model's geometry.

parameters.description: Explicit snapshot(s) and project/building scope; do not combine overlapping revisions as additional objects.
Selected building/system/package and maintainability criteria.
Versioned required documents and applicability criteria.

steps.pseudocode: Select identified assets under explicit maintainability and scope criteria; report uncertain identity, classification or location separately.
Assess supplied applicable handover requirements against evidenced links; a document link does not itself establish document adequacy.
Return readable location and references to appropriate representations for requested assets; unknown geometry does not erase the asset.

workflows.missingDataBehavior: Unknown maintainability is not automatically excluded; expose it as a classification gap. Missing location or manuals remain explicit. Unmatched source objects are not automatically merged.
workflows.countingBasis: One identified asset occurrence in selected delivery scope; type records, reusable meshes and duplicate representations are not extra assets.
acceptanceExamples: Synthetic: an asset with a known room but no geometry appears in the register and can have an incomplete manual requirement.
Synthetic: two confirmed source records for one asset produce one asset-register entry.
openQuestions: External document identity, warranties, maintenance requirements and document adequacy checks need dedicated contracts.
What asset classifications and required handover fields should lead?

workflows.title: Package readiness
workflows.question: Which packages lack decisions or delivery evidence needed to proceed?
workflows.decision: Prioritize readiness blockers and identify the schedule or delivery information needed before committing work.

parameters.description: Explicit snapshot(s) and building/project scope, including non-overlap rules for revisions.
Applicable scope, named measurement/assessment rules and external scenario inputs.

steps.pseudocode: Select package scope; summarize supported blockers and unknown readiness. Modeled geometry does not establish readiness.

workflows.missingDataBehavior: Return supported partial facts and unresolved scope. Milestones, dependencies, responsibility and readiness policies need explicit contracts.
workflows.countingBasis: One package; overlapping object assignments are not independent progress.
acceptanceExamples: Synthetic: A package with no required delivery evidence remains readiness-unknown.

parameters.description: Explicit snapshot(s) and building/project scope, including non-overlap rules for revisions.
Applicable scope, named measurement/assessment rules and external scenario inputs.

steps.pseudocode: In a resolved common frame, filter envelopes by the requested region; deduplicate object identities. Return candidates for exact geometric testing, not confirmed clashes.

workflows.countingBasis: One unordered object pair per rule; duplicate meshes do not multiply findings.
acceptanceExamples: Synthetic: Bounds overlap alone is a candidate, not a confirmed clash.
